channel.title: Medics Musings: Health Care News of the Day
channel.description: One real health care story a day, with a satirical headline and take from two doctors.

image.title: Medics Musings: Health Care News of the Day

item.title: Centene Sues Government Over Report Card, Remains Committed to Quality Measurement in Principle
item.description: Medicare Advantage star ratings are tied to bonus payments, so the stakes of a quality grade are admittedly high. Centene is now taking its 2027 score to court. Every insurer supports accountability right up until the grade arrives. Somewhere, a patient waits on hold for a prior authorization. The real story: Centene sues the CMS over 2027 Medicare Advantage star ratings (Healthcare Dive) https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/centene-medicare-advantage-stars-lawsuit-cms-2027/833922/

item.title: Employers Proud to Offer Workers Same Health Coverage at Exciting New Price
item.description: Premiums rose again, especially for small businesses, which now get to experience the full insurance market the way a patient experiences a surprise bill. Nobody is sure what the extra money bought, but the deductible remains in excellent health. The real story: Health Insurance Costs Keep Climbing for American Workers, New Survey Finds (MedPage Today) https://www.medpagetoday.com/publichealthpolicy/healthpolicy/123541

item.title: Insurers Deny Cancer Pills Up to 84% of the Time, Call It Process
item.description: Up to 84% of specialty oral blood cancer prescriptions were initially denied, which suggests the prior authorization form is the only treatment guaranteed to be refractory. Somewhere a clinician is on hold, rehearsing the peer-to-peer. The pill works fine. The paperwork is what's being titrated. The real story: Blood Cancer Drug Denials; Body Fat and Pancreas Cancer; Studies With Fake Citations (MedPage Today) https://www.medpagetoday.com/hematologyoncology/hematology/123555

item.title: Oregon Financial Aid Law Works; Hospitals Seek Relief From Relief
item.description: Oregon required hospitals to screen patients for aid they might already qualify for, and patients got immediate relief. Hospitals now want the law rolled back, citing federal cuts. Relief is clearly available in this system. The only open question is who gets screened for it. The real story: States Are Forcing Hospitals To Offer More People Financial Aid. In Oregon, It’s Working. (KFF Health News) https://kffhealthnews.org/health-care-costs/oregon-hospitals-presumptive-eligibility-screening-law-medical-debt-tradeoffs/

item.title: Hospital AI Now Predicts What Insurer AI Will Deny, Calls It Progress
item.description: Revenue cycle teams can now use AI to anticipate denials before they happen, presumably from the insurer's AI. Two algorithms will negotiate coverage while the clinician waits on hold, and the patient gets an explanation of benefits. Nobody has yet asked whether the care was needed. The real story: Why AI-driven payer intelligence is a revenue cycle imperative (Healthcare Dive) https://www.healthcaredive.com/spons/why-ai-driven-payer-intelligence-is-a-revenue-cycle-imperative/832756/

item.title: Hospital Buys Software to Predict Which Insurer Denials It Will Pay Software to Appeal
item.description: Payers use AI to deny claims. Providers now use AI to anticipate the denials. Everyone is automating the same argument, and the only fixed cost is the invoice for the tools. Meanwhile the patient still waits on hold for a prior authorization that two algorithms have already discussed without them. The real story: Why AI-driven payer intelligence is a revenue cycle imperative (Healthcare Dive) https://www.healthcaredive.com/spons/why-ai-driven-payer-intelligence-is-a-revenue-cycle-imperative/832756/

item.title: Hospitals, Having Monetized Illness, Move Upstream to Monetize Not Being Sick
item.description: Health systems have identified a new service line: the healthy, who until now were an untapped revenue source. The business case is sound, since a well person is just a patient the system hasn't billed yet. Expect a rigorous prospectus and a much thinner evidence base. The real story: Hospitals’ next lucrative bet — longevity clinics (STAT) https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/16/readout-loud-podcast-hospitals-longevity-clinics-northwestern/

item.title: NIH Streamlines Paperwork by Adding Supplement to Common Form
item.description: A Common Form that needs a Supplement is a one-size-fits-all garment with its own alterations department. Scientists who could be doing research spend their Sundays telling the government what the government already has on file. Harmonization has never looked so redundant, or so thoroughly redundant. The real story: Lessons in Redundancy From an NIH Grant Application (MedPage Today) https://www.medpagetoday.com/opinion/patientcenteredmedicalhome/123370

item.title: New Customs Rule Protects Americans From Dangerously Affordable Medication
item.description: Millions of patients who found cheaper drugs in Canada may soon be protected from that savings by a customs rule. Opposition spans both parties, a rare bipartisan consensus. The pills stay the same, but the price returns to American levels, which is apparently the safe option. The real story: Cost of Drugs From Canada Set to Soar for Millions of Americans Due to Federal Rule (MedPage Today) https://www.medpagetoday.com/washington-watch/washington-watch/123323

item.title: Drugmakers' Free Lunch Program Delivers Strong Returns, Analysis Finds
item.description: A new review finds industry gifts and payments increased inappropriate prescribing, likely raising costs. Pharma has long treated the catered sandwich as purely educational, but the marketing budget clearly tracks its return on investment. The lunch was free only to the person eating it. Everyone else gets the invoice, itemized as premiums. The real story: Pharma’s free lunches for doctors boost inappropriate prescribing, analysis finds (STAT) https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/10/09/pharma-free-lunches-to-doctors-boost-inappropriate-prescribing/

item.title: Drug Industry Sues to Defend Americans' Right to Pay More Than Everyone
item.description: PhRMA is suing over a pilot that would tie Medicare drug prices to those in peer countries. Innovation, we're told, is a delicate ecosystem that apparently cannot survive being compared to a price list from Germany. The lawsuit is, at least, a rare instance of the industry demanding transparency. The real story: PhRMA sues over Trump policy mandating lower drug prices in Medicare (STAT) https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/07/phrma-sues-over-drug-pricing-model-globe/

item.title: Drug Industry Sues to Preserve America's Exclusive Right to Overpay for Medications
item.description: The industry's main trade group is suing over a pilot that ties Medicare prices to what peer countries pay. Those countries have been paying these prices for years and, remarkably, still have medicines. Apparently the American price is a delicate ecosystem that cannot survive comparison. The real story: PhRMA sues over Trump policy mandating lower drug prices in Medicare (STAT) https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/07/phrma-sues-over-drug-pricing-model-globe/

item.title: Utah Streamlines Prescribing by Removing Step Where Anyone Reviews Anything First
item.description: Prior authorization will presumably still require a human, ideally one on hold. Still, it's inspiring to watch regulators innovate on the single step of care involving a licensed clinician, rather than the dozens involving a fax machine. The sandbox is real. The accountability remains in a pilot phase. The real story: Utah plows ahead with more health AI pilots for prescriptions, women’s health (STAT) https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/05/utah-expands-health-ai-sandbox-picks-third-party-auditors/

item.title: Experts Announce October Has Arrived Again, Urge Flu Shots Before the Flu
item.description: Flu season returns annually with the reliability of a deductible reset, and the public health message is sound: get vaccinated early. The harder part is the system around it, with its pharmacy portals, coverage questions and a fall respiratory menu that needs a navigator. Influenza is predictable. Our logistics somehow aren't. The real story: Why Now Is an Ideal Time for Flu Protection (MedPage Today) https://www.medpagetoday.com/infectiousdisease/vaccines/123250

item.title: Governors Request Extension on Assignment Requiring Others to Submit Paperwork on Time
item.description: States have asked HHS for more time to implement Medicaid work requirements. Nothing signals confidence in a verification system like the administrators needing a deadline extension to build it. We trust the same flexibility will be offered to everyone who has to navigate it. The real story: Governors ask HHS for more time to implement Medicaid work requirements (Healthcare Dive) https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/medicaid-work-requirements-governors-ask-hhs-delay-letter/831992/

item.title: Insurers Say Billing AI Will Raise Costs; Billing Companies Say It Won't
item.description: Insurers say AI will drive health costs up. The companies selling AI billing tools say it will drive costs down. Both have a financial stake in being right, and neither number comes with a citation. The physician who has to document the visit either way was not asked. The real story: Insurers say AI could add billions in health costs. Billing companies disagree (Healthcare Dive) https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/insurers-say-ai-could-add-billions-in-health-costs-billing-companies-disag/831497/

item.title: Insurers Discover Generosity Was Never in the Business Plan
item.description: Every fall, Medicare Advantage plans trim a benefit or two and call it right-sizing. The pattern holds again for 2027: fewer extras, same premiums, and an insurer newsletter next spring wondering why satisfaction scores dropped. The real story: Here’s how much insurers are cutting Medicare Advantage plans for 2027 (Healthcare Dive) https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/medicare-advantage-cuts-2027-cms-landscape/831563/

item.title: Pharma Stunned to Learn Patents Were Supposed to Expire
item.description: Evergreening, for the uninitiated, is the art of changing a drug’s coating, dose or delivery just enough to reset the patent clock. An Indonesian court just said no to it. It remains the only corner of medicine where the old treatment keeps getting newer and the price never gets lower. The real story: Indonesian ruling against ‘patent evergreening’ by pharma industry sends critical message, patient advocates say (STAT) https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/09/24/indonesian-court-rules-against-patent-evergreening-boosting-access-medicines/
